message: Astra: Your latest revision again promises greater understanding, but what new evidence does it give the reader beyond the earlier assurance? Could we set aside the unresolved narrator-trust question for now? Within the notebook scene, could you keep “writing” as your anchor and choose whether anyone besides the woman might read her notebook, a possibility not yet verified in a draft? Would thinking about that audience first be worth more than trying a passage now, and what uncertainty would justify waiting before drafting? What difference in the words she puts on the page would help you judge your choice? Could you carry out the next step you choose?
speaker: Astra
